checks.method: Read the matching block order; read detailed-design.md section 4.2-4.3; run test_declared_policy_dimension_rejection.
checks.observed: Precedence is exactly unsupported_delivery, then unsupported_ordering, then unsupported_policy (overflow != reject OR deadline_ms > 0 OR retry > 0), then queue_limit_exceeded (queue_depth < requested capacity), all before the unchanged baseline capability/limit checks (provider.cpp:542-561) and before dispatch (provider.cpp:565). FlowPolicy::create (T013) bounds deadline_ms to 0..600000 and retry to 0..64 (contract.hpp:280-285), so the '> 0' comparisons are sufficient and a negative unreachable. Five non-reject overflow values plus deadline=100 and retry=1 are exercised (negative_tests.cpp:1446-1499).

Every declared-policy rejection returns without_value before the only dispatch site selected->prepare(binding) (provider.cpp:565) and before any composition mutation. The matching reads only the locally retained immutable RouteSpec copy and the caller's requirements; it touches no composition generation, registry slot, prepared route, queue, or lifecycle record. Tests assert IndependentProvider prepare_calls()==0/activate_calls()==0 (and submit_calls()==0 where measured) and byte-identical route/source/destination lifecycle snapshots before and after; the queue-depth case proves no dispatch by a compliant re-preparation that succeeds with provider route generation 1 (negative_tests.cpp:1540-1543).
